title: Luzzatto's middle rungs, zeal to purity
hookLine: zeal, cleanliness, separation, purity: the middle rungs
carry: zeal to purity: the Merciful One wants the heart
tomorrow: A little holy below, much from above

lines: EACH STEP BECAUSE THE LAST ONE HELD.
cards: Old stone staircases wear down in the middle of each step. Not at the edges, not at the top. Right where feet land, one after another, for years, each step taken because the one below it held.
Nobody reaches the top of those stairs in a single jump, and nobody wore them down in a day. Luzzatto's ladder has rungs like that. Yesterday was the bottom one, watchfulness.
Today is the climb through the middle, where the ordinary work of character happens.

teach.b: Step by step. Four middle rungs from Mesillat Yesharim, in the order Luzzatto climbs them. First, zeal.
Zerizut, which this path met earlier: doing the good thing promptly instead of later. Watchfulness sees what to do; zeal gets up and does it. Second, cleanliness.

Luzzatto means being clean of the small faults that hide in the corners, the little dishonesties and shortcuts a person stops noticing because they seem like what everyone does. Cleanliness goes looking in the cracks.
Now the question is no longer what's forbidden but how much of what's allowed. The Talmud has a short line for it: sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you. Not giving up the world.
Choosing not to take every permitted thing just because you can. One less scroll, one less helping, one less purchase, on purpose. Fourth, purity.
Taharah. This rung turns inward, to motive: doing the right thing for the right reason, not for credit.

teach.h: PURITY: THE MERCIFUL ONE WANTS THE HEART.
teach.b: The Talmud says it in a few words: the Merciful One wants the heart. And the recent days, read as stairs: speaking good, after guarding speech. Anger, cooled before it speaks.
Envy, set down. The benefit of the doubt. Then the path of the just, watchfulness, and now these middle rungs.
You don't need to see the top to take the step in front of you.

how: Mussar students work through the traits of Mesillat Yesharim in order, after watchfulness: zeal, cleanliness, separation and purity, often focusing on one trait for a stretch of weeks.

o: a set of rules kept all at once
a quick leap straight to holiness
climbing the traits one rung at a time

games.q: step by step — tap the pairs.
p: zeal: do the good thing now

s: nekiut means being clean of small faults that hide in the corners.
separation means giving up the world
the Talmud's line is sanctify yourself in what is permitted: choosing less, not leaving.
the Talmud says the Merciful One wants the heart.

games.q: your life looks fine from the outside: you're prompt, honest in small things, and you skip some permitted extras. what does the next rung, purity, ask?
o: look at why you're doing them.
games.why: purity turns inward, to motive: the Merciful One wants the heart.

practice: Pick one ordinary daily habit, how you answer messages, eat lunch, or end the evening, and walk it up the rungs: a good part you keep putting off, a small shortcut hiding in it, a permitted extra you could leave out, and why you do it at all.
You don't need four changes; choose the smallest real step and hold it until it feels doable. If you pray, you can ask for help with that one step.

wordCard.voice: Step by step. Zeal, cleanliness, separation, purity: the middle rungs of Luzzatto's ladder, each resting on the one below. Today's word.
